blocks.source: 【RPG制作講座】自由度
blocks.translation: RPG Design Guides: Freedom

blocks.source: 一般に自由度が高いＲＰＧは良いＲＰＧであると言われることが多い。逆に自由度が低いＲＰＧ――例えばＦＦ１３などは「一本道」「ロールプレイングならぬレールプレイングゲームだ」というように、非難を浴びることが多い。
blocks.translation: RPGs with a high degree of freedom are often considered good RPGs. Conversely, RPGs with little freedom—such as FF13—are frequently criticized as being “linear” or “rail-playing games rather than role-playing games.”

blocks.source: ネット上でのレビューや議論を見る限りでは、どうやらみんな『自由度』が大好きなようだ。
blocks.translation: Judging from reviews and discussions online, it seems that everyone loves “freedom.”

blocks.source: そんな自由度であるが、そこに含まれる『自由』の内実は多岐に渡る。
blocks.translation: However, the nature of the “freedom” encompassed by this concept varies widely.

blocks.source: 行き先を決める自由
blocks.translation: The freedom to choose where to go

blocks.source: 誰を仲間にするか決める自由
blocks.translation: The freedom to choose whom to recruit

blocks.source: 村人に話しかける自由
blocks.translation: The freedom to talk to villagers

blocks.source: 気に入らないイベントに参加しない自由
blocks.translation: The freedom to skip events you do not like

blocks.source: というようにだ。
blocks.translation: And so on.

blocks.source: そこで、今一度『自由』というものを細分化しまとめる。自由の内実を理解することで、自由の一体何が面白いのかに迫ってみたい。そして、ゲームが面白くなる方向に自由度を調整できるようになりたいところだ。
blocks.translation: So, I would like to break down and summarize the concept of “freedom” once again. By understanding what freedom actually consists of, I want to explore what makes it interesting. Ideally, I would also like to become able to adjust the degree of freedom in ways that make games more interesting.

blocks.source: 目次
blocks.translation: Table of Contents

blocks.source: 二つの自由
blocks.translation: Two Types of Freedom

blocks.source: ゲームにおける自由とは、大きく二つに分けることができる。『目的の自由』と『手段の自由』である。
blocks.translation: Freedom in games can be broadly divided into two types: “freedom of objectives” and “freedom of means.”

blocks.source: 目的の自由
blocks.translation: Freedom of Objectives

blocks.source: プレイヤーが目的を決めることができるという自由。例えば、マルチエンディングの作品で、どのエンディングを目指すのかを決めるといった自由だ。
blocks.translation: The freedom to choose one’s objectives. For example, in a game with multiple endings, this means being free to decide which ending to pursue.

blocks.source: 目的といっても、個別のイベントの目的から、物語の最終目的まで幅広い。洋ゲーなどはこの辺の自由度も高いらしいが、良く知らないので省略。
blocks.translation: Objectives can range from the goal of an individual event to the story’s ultimate objective. Western games apparently offer a high degree of freedom in this area as well, but I am not familiar enough with them, so I will leave that out.

blocks.source: ポケモンで「ストーリーのクリアはタダの通過点。目的は対戦で勝ちまくることだ！」というのも、立派な目的の自由。
blocks.translation: In Pokémon, saying “Clearing the story is just a stepping stone. My goal is to win as many battles as possible!” is also a fine example of freedom of objectives.

blocks.source: ただし、これが全くの自由だと「何をやったら良いのか分からない」という状態になりやすいので注意。かくいう僕も「何でもできる」だけのゲームをやるぐらいなら、リアルで創作活動でもしてたほうがいいんじゃね？ とか思っていたりする。
blocks.translation: However, be careful: if this freedom is completely unrestricted, players can easily end up not knowing what they are supposed to do. Personally, I sometimes think that if I am going to play a game where “you can do anything,” I might as well pursue creative activities in the real world instead.

blocks.source: やはり、ある程度の方向性は示して欲しいところ。
blocks.translation: I still want the game to point me in a general direction.

blocks.source: 手段の自由
blocks.translation: Freedom of Means

blocks.source: 目的は確定しているものとする。その上で目的を果たすための手段の自由を指す。
blocks.translation: Assume that the objective has already been determined. This refers to the freedom to choose the means of accomplishing it.

blocks.source: 例えば、敵のボスを「力尽くで倒すか」「トラップを仕掛けてからめ手で倒すか」それとも「交渉して和解するか」といったものだ。
blocks.translation: For example, deciding whether to defeat an enemy boss “by force,” “by setting a trap and using an underhanded tactic,” or “by negotiating and reaching a peaceful agreement.”

blocks.source: 例として……
blocks.translation: For example…

blocks.source: バンガード（ロマンシングサガ３）
blocks.translation: Vanguard (Romancing SaGa 3)

blocks.source: 潜水機能を持った要塞バンガードを起動するという目的のために、術師の協力を得ることに。しかし、有力な二人の術師は仲が悪い上に、タダでは力を貸してくれそうにない。
blocks.translation: To achieve the objective of activating Vanguard, a fortress equipped for underwater travel, you must enlist the help of a spellcaster. However, the two most capable spellcasters dislike each other, and neither seems willing to lend their power for free.

blocks.source: 取りうる選択肢は以下のようになる。
blocks.translation: The available options are as follows.

blocks.source: 術師Ａを倒して、術師Ｂの協力を得る。
blocks.translation: Defeat Spellcaster A and obtain Spellcaster B’s cooperation.

blocks.source: 術師Ｂを倒して、術師Ａの協力を得る。
blocks.translation: Defeat Spellcaster B and obtain Spellcaster A’s cooperation.

blocks.source: 喧嘩両成敗にして、両方の協力を得る。
blocks.translation: Punish both sides equally and obtain the cooperation of both.

blocks.source: アイスソード（ロマンシングサガ）
blocks.translation: The Ice Sword (Romancing SaGa)

blocks.source: 終盤のダンジョンである冥府に向かうためには、火山の主と交渉しなくてはならない。「アイスソードを持ってくれば通してやる」とのことだが、剣の持ち主である聖戦士も簡単には譲ってくれそうにない。
blocks.translation: To reach the late-game dungeon known as the Underworld, you must negotiate with the lord of the volcano. He says, “Bring me the Ice Sword and I’ll let you pass,” but the holy warrior who owns the sword is not likely to give it up easily either.

blocks.source: 手段の自由度が高い作品は工夫の余地も大きく、戦略性が高い作品と言えるかもしれない。シナリオ側だけではなくゲームシステム・バランス側の分担も大事だ。
blocks.translation: Games with a high degree of freedom in their means leave plenty of room for ingenuity and could be considered highly strategic. The scenario design is important, but so is the game system and balance.

blocks.source: 詳細な自由
blocks.translation: Detailed Types of Freedom

blocks.source: 以下は上に挙げた２つの自由をより詳細に分類したもの。
blocks.translation: Below is a more detailed classification of the two types of freedom mentioned above.

blocks.source: 選択の自由
blocks.translation: Freedom of Choice

blocks.source: 掲示された選択肢を選ぶ自由。
blocks.translation: The freedom to choose from the options presented.

blocks.source: 場合によっては、上に挙げたような目的や手段が変化することもある。
blocks.translation: Depending on the situation, the objectives and means mentioned above may also change.

blocks.source: 印象的なのはタクティクスオウガ。この作品では要所の選択肢に対する決定によって、以降の展開が大きく変化する。
blocks.translation: Tactics Ogre is particularly memorable in this regard. In this game, decisions made at key points can dramatically change what happens afterward.

blocks.source: 特に一章最後の選択肢では、主人公が悪事に加担することもできるという内容で、当時衝撃的だった。
blocks.translation: The choice at the end of Chapter One was especially shocking at the time, as it allowed the protagonist to become involved in wrongdoing.

blocks.source: このように自分の判断がストーリー展開を大きく左右するということは、プレイヤーの作品への没入感を強く高める。複数の展開を用意するのは、やはり手間が掛かるのだが……。
blocks.translation: When your own decisions have a major impact on the story’s progression in this way, it greatly increases the player’s immersion in the game. Of course, preparing multiple story routes takes a lot of work…

blocks.source: ドラクエによくあるような『はい』だろうが『いいえ』だろうが、会話内容がちょっと変わる程度でしかない選択肢だってもちろん『選択の自由』の一部。結果は変わらないという点で、さほど自由度に寄与しているとは言えないかもしれないが……。
blocks.translation: Choices like those commonly found in Dragon Quest, where answering “Yes” or “No” only slightly changes the dialogue, are of course also part of the “freedom of choice.” Since the outcome does not change, they may not contribute much to the overall degree of freedom, though…

blocks.source: 行動範囲の自由
blocks.translation: Freedom of Movement

blocks.source: 「どれだけ広い範囲を移動できるか」「どれだけ遠くまで移動できるか」「どんな場所に行けるのか」といった自由。
blocks.translation: The freedom to decide “how large an area you can move around in,” “how far you can travel,” and “what kinds of places you can visit.”

blocks.source: ストーリーを進めることで、行動範囲が広がるのが普通だ。特に乗物入手による移動範囲の拡張はワクワクもの。
blocks.translation: It is normal for the range of movement to expand as the story progresses. In particular, obtaining a vehicle and thereby expanding the area you can travel is exciting.

blocks.source: 自由度が高いＲＰＧは序盤から行動範囲の制約がゆるい傾向にある。これが極めてゆるい作品は、特にオープンワールドなんて呼ばれたりする。
blocks.translation: RPGs with a high degree of freedom tend to place few restrictions on movement from the early stages. Games with exceptionally loose restrictions are often called open-world games.

blocks.source: 最初から制約はほとんどないが、遠出すると敵が強くなるので実質的には制約があるというＤＱ１型もある。
blocks.translation: There is also the Dragon Quest I model: there are almost no restrictions from the beginning, but enemies become stronger when you travel farther, creating practical restrictions.

blocks.source: このタイプの場合、ストーリーを進めなくとも、プレイヤーのスキル次第で遠出できるという利点がある。
blocks.translation: The advantage of this type is that, even without progressing the story, players can travel far depending on their skill.

blocks.source: 自由度が低いＲＰＧの場合は、前の町に戻ることも満足にできなかったりする。やはりＦＦ１３の一本道などが代表的。
blocks.translation: In RPGs with little freedom, you may not even be able to return properly to previous towns. FF13’s linear progression is once again a representative example.

blocks.source: それに限らず、ストーリー性重視のＲＰＧならば、一時的に行動範囲が狭まった結果、一本道になりやすい。
blocks.translation: More generally, in RPGs that prioritize storytelling, the range of movement may temporarily narrow, making the game more likely to become linear.

blocks.source: 移動手段の便利さも重要だ。
blocks.translation: The convenience of the available means of transportation is also important.

blocks.source: 移動呪文ルーラがあるＤＱシリーズや、ワールドマップを開けば一瞬で各地に移動できるロマサガなどは便利。近年ではファストトラベルなんて言葉が一般的になってもいる。
blocks.translation: The Dragon Quest series, with its Zoom spell, and Romancing SaGa, where opening the world map lets you travel anywhere in an instant, are convenient. In recent years, the term “fast travel” has also become commonplace.

blocks.source: 前の町に戻るのに、非常に時間がかかるような仕様では、わざわざ面倒をかけてまで戻ることは少ないだろう。これもやはり一本道に近いプレイになりやすい。
blocks.translation: If it takes an extremely long time to return to a previous town, players are unlikely to go back out of their way. This, too, tends to result in gameplay that is nearly linear.

blocks.source: 施設／システムを利用する自由
blocks.translation: Freedom to Use Facilities and Systems

blocks.source: 「お店を始めとした施設を利用できるか」「どんな道具・装備を購入できるか」「転職などのシステムを利用できるか」「どんな職業に転職できるか」といった自由。
blocks.translation: The freedom to choose things such as “whether you can use facilities including shops,” “what items and equipment you can purchase,” “whether you can use systems such as changing jobs,” and “which jobs you can change to.”

blocks.source: ストーリーの進行によって、利用できる『施設／システム』がぎちぎちに定められている場合、戦略の幅が狭まることになる。
blocks.translation: If the facilities and systems available to the player are rigidly restricted according to story progression, the range of possible strategies becomes narrower.

blocks.source: かといって、序盤から何でもできてしまうと、何をやってよいのか分からなくなる。さらには中盤・後半にモチベーションとなる要素がなくなってしまう問題もある。ここはゲームバランスのセンスが要求される大事な部分だ。
blocks.translation: On the other hand, if you can do anything from the beginning, you may not know what you are supposed to do. Another problem is that there may be nothing left to motivate you during the middle and latter parts of the game. This is an important area that requires a good sense of game balance.

blocks.source: 順序の自由
blocks.translation: Freedom of Order

blocks.source: イベント等をどんな順番にこなすかを決定する自由。
blocks.translation: The freedom to decide the order in which to complete events and the like.

blocks.source: ＤＱシリーズには大抵、オーブなどの何かを自由な順序で集めるイベントがある。ロマサガ２の七英雄退治、ロマサガ３の四魔貴族退治などもこれ。ＪＲＰＧにおける自由度が高い作品は、これが充実している場合が多い。
blocks.translation: The Dragon Quest series usually includes events where you collect something, such as orbs, in any order you like. This also applies to defeating the Seven Heroes in Romancing SaGa 2 and the Four Sinistrals in Romancing SaGa 3. JRPGs with a high degree of freedom often make extensive use of this approach.

blocks.source: 「順番を変えられるだけじゃ大したことない」「所詮は朝三暮四」なんて思われるかもしれないが、これがなかなか侮れない。
blocks.translation: You may think, “Being able to change the order isn’t a big deal,” or “It’s just a superficial change,” but this is surprisingly significant.

blocks.source: 例えば、この自由によってどんなことができるかというと……
blocks.translation: For example, here are some things you can do with this freedom...

blocks.source: 敵が強いダンジョンにあえて挑んで、パーティを効率良く強化する。
blocks.translation: Challenge a dungeon with particularly strong enemies in order to strengthen your party efficiently.

blocks.source: 良い武器がある町に優先して向かう。
blocks.translation: Prioritize visiting towns that have good weapons.

blocks.source: 炎のボスと戦う前に、弱点の氷の武器が手に入るイベントをこなす。ロックマン式。
blocks.translation: Complete the event that gives you an ice weapon, the fire boss’s weakness, before fighting it. The Mega Man approach.

blocks.source: 気に入った仲間が加わるイベントを優先してこなす。
blocks.translation: Prioritize events that add companions you like.

blocks.source: 一通り行動できる範囲をブラブラしてみて、面白そうなイベントに挑む。
blocks.translation: Wander around the areas you can access and challenge whichever events look interesting.

blocks.source: というように、意外とプレイの幅が広がるものだ。
blocks.translation: As you can see, this can broaden the range of gameplay more than you might expect.

blocks.source: もっとも初回プレイではどこで望みの物が手に入るかを把握するのは難しいのだが、色んな場所に手探りで行ってみるのも楽しいもの。二周目以降はどうやればプレイ効率を上げられるかを考える楽しみもある。
blocks.translation: Of course, on your first playthrough it is difficult to know where to find the things you want, but it can be fun to explore various places and feel your way around. From the second playthrough onward, there is also the pleasure of figuring out how to improve your efficiency.

blocks.source: もちろん『行動範囲の自由』が大きいほど、比例してこちらも大きくなるので、合わせて考えよう。
blocks.translation: Naturally, the greater your “freedom of movement,” the greater this freedom becomes as well, so keep the two in mind together.

blocks.source: 任意の自由
blocks.translation: Optional Freedom

blocks.source: やってもやらなくてもよいという自由。
blocks.translation: The freedom to do something—or not do it.

blocks.source: ゲームクリアに必須ではないサブイベントがこれに当たる。話しかける必要がない町人との会話も、これに含むと考えることができる。任意とは言っても重要度の高さに応じてその意味合いも変わってくる。
blocks.translation: This includes side events that are not necessary to complete the game. Conversations with townspeople whom you do not need to speak to can also be considered part of this category. Although they are optional, their significance changes depending on how important they are.

blocks.source: 重要度が高いと……
blocks.translation: When It Is Highly Important...

blocks.source: 進行上重要で、こなさないと進行に支障を来たす。
blocks.translation: It is important for progressing the game, and failing to complete it interferes with your progress.

blocks.source: 例えば「ハッピーエンドのフラグが立たない」「攻略に必要な情報が不足する」など、事実上の半強制に近いことも。
blocks.translation: For example, it may be practically semi-mandatory if “the happy ending flag is never set” or “you lack information necessary for completing the game.”

blocks.source: ＤＱ３においては、ラスボス弱体化に必要な『光の玉』の入手イベントがこれに当たる。
blocks.translation: In Dragon Quest III, the event where you obtain the “Sphere of Light,” which is needed to weaken the final boss, falls into this category.

blocks.source: 重要度が低いと……
blocks.translation: When It Is of Low Importance...

blocks.source: 別にやらなくてもよい。「強力な装備が手に入るが、無くても十分クリアできる」「キャラクターの個別エピソード。本編にはさほど関係ない」など。
blocks.translation: You do not really need to do it. Examples include “you can obtain powerful equipment, but you can easily complete the game without it” and “individual character episodes that have little to do with the main story.”

blocks.source: またまたＤＱ３に例えると、『ノアニール』や『ムオル』のイベントがこれに当たる。そんなイベント知らね・忘れたって人はごめんなさい。
blocks.translation: To use Dragon Quest III as an example once again, the events in “Noaniels” and “Muor” fall into this category. Sorry to anyone thinking, “I don’t know those events,” or “I forgot about them.”

blocks.source: 自由度とゲーム性
blocks.translation: Freedom and Gameplay

blocks.source: 一般に「自由度が高い作品はゲーム性も高い」と言われる傾向にある。取り得る選択肢が豊富にあるため、戦術性も高くなるためだ。サガシリーズなどはその典型だろう。
blocks.translation: It is generally said that “games with a high degree of freedom also have strong gameplay.” This is because having many options available also increases the tactical depth. The SaGa series is probably a typical example.

blocks.source: ただし、自由度とゲーム性は必ずしも両立しない。
blocks.translation: However, freedom and gameplay do not necessarily go hand in hand.

blocks.source: 例えば、あるダンジョンの敵を強くすると必然的に探索が難しくなる。早期の攻略が困難になるという意味では、これは自由度を下げる調整である。
blocks.translation: For example, making the enemies in a dungeon stronger inevitably makes exploration more difficult. In the sense that it makes completing the dungeon early more difficult, this is an adjustment that reduces freedom.

blocks.source: 逆に、ダンジョンの敵を弱くすれば自由度は上がるのだが、プレイヤーが攻略する楽しみは薄くなってしまう。自由度を上げた結果、ゲーム性が下がったとも言えるわけだ。
blocks.translation: Conversely, weakening the enemies in a dungeon increases freedom, but it also diminishes the fun of overcoming the dungeon. In other words, increasing freedom can result in lower-quality gameplay.

blocks.source: 当然ながら「障害がない」ということは「攻略の必要もない」ということでもある。ゲーム性を追求するなら、やはり一定の制約も必要だろう。
blocks.translation: Naturally, “having no obstacles” also means “having no need to overcome anything.” If you want to pursue strong gameplay, a certain degree of restriction is necessary.

blocks.source: 極端な話をすれば「どのシナリオからでも自由に攻略できます！ 順序による有利不利はありません！」というゲームデザインは「順序が自由なだけの短編集」に限りなく近くなっていく。
blocks.translation: To take this to an extreme, a game design that says, “You can complete any scenario you like! There are no advantages or disadvantages based on order!” will come very close to being “an anthology of short stories whose only distinguishing feature is that they can be played in any order.”

blocks.source: 攻略のしがいは薄くなるし、シナリオに順序がないから壮大なストーリーも作りにくい。盛り上がりのある作品を作るには苦労しそうだ。
blocks.translation: There is less incentive to overcome challenges, and because the scenarios have no fixed order, it is also difficult to create an epic story. Creating a game with exciting developments would likely be challenging.

blocks.source: そういう作品もあっていいとは思うけれど、理想のゲームデザインかと言われると考えものだろう。
blocks.translation: I think it is fine for games like that to exist, but whether they represent an ideal game design is another matter.

blocks.source: 自由に対する結果・反応
blocks.translation: Results and Responses to Player Freedom

blocks.source: 最後に『結果』『反応』の重要性を指摘しておきたい。
blocks.translation: Finally, I would like to point out the importance of “results” and “responses.”

blocks.source: 自由とは第一にプレイヤーが何をできるかという『入力』である。しかし、入力の方法が豊富なだけでは、十分な自由度が得られるとは言い難い。
blocks.translation: Freedom is first and foremost the “input” of what the player can do. However, simply having many ways to provide input does not necessarily result in a sufficient degree of freedom.

blocks.source: 自由度の高さを実感するには、入力に対する『出力』――つまり『結果』『反応』が必要なのだ。これが充実していないことにはどんなに入力が豊富でも、見せかけの自由でしかない。
blocks.translation: To truly feel a high degree of freedom, you need “output” in response to the input—in other words, “results” and “responses.” Without enough of this, no matter how many inputs are available, it is only the appearance of freedom.

blocks.source: 例を挙げてみよう。
blocks.translation: Let me give you an example.

blocks.source: 「ＤＱ３の勇者は２１１６８通りの装備ができる！
blocks.translation: “The Luminary in Dragon Quest III can equip 21,168 different combinations!

blocks.source: だからＤＱ３の装備は自由度が超高い！」
blocks.translation: Therefore, Dragon Quest III’s equipment system offers an incredibly high degree of freedom!”

blocks.source: ※ＦＣ版「武器：２１ × 鎧：１８ × 盾：８ × 兜：７」で算出。
blocks.translation: ※Calculated for the FC version as “Weapons: 21 × Armor: 18 × Shields: 8 × Helmets: 7.”

blocks.source: 装飾品は無視。女性専用装備と素手含む。
blocks.translation: Accessories are excluded. Female-only equipment and bare hands are included.

blocks.source: 恐らく、この主張に納得してくれる人はほとんどいないはず。それは２１１６８の内、意味のある組み合わせ自体がほとんど限られているからである。
blocks.translation: Presumably, very few people would agree with this claim. That is because only a very limited number of those 21,168 combinations are actually meaningful.

blocks.source: ＤＱ９では装備品によって、キャラクターの見た目が変わるのだが、この時点ではそういった要素も見られない。
blocks.translation: In Dragon Quest IX, a character’s appearance changes depending on their equipment, but even that kind of element is not present here.

blocks.source: よって、性能に優れた装備だけで固めるのが常となる。
blocks.translation: As a result, players generally end up equipping only the equipment with the best performance.

blocks.source: 「武器は王者の剣――ただし防具は全裸」
blocks.translation: “The weapon is the King’s Sword—but the armor is being completely naked.”

blocks.source: というような珍妙な組み合わせは、最初から選択肢にも入らないというわけだ。
blocks.translation: In other words, bizarre combinations like that are not even options to begin with.

blocks.source: 要するに自由度が高いとは「プレイヤーが取るに値する行動パターンが豊富にあること」を意味している。そういう意味では『戦略性』『戦術性』にも通じる部分がある。
blocks.translation: In short, a high degree of freedom means “having a wide variety of action patterns that are worth choosing for the player.” In that sense, it also has something in common with “strategic depth” and “tactical depth.”

blocks.source: そのためにも、重要なのはバランス調整だ。
blocks.translation: That is why balance adjustment is so important.

blocks.source: 「性能に大差ない仲間キャラが大量にいる自由」「弱い武器を買う自由」「ダルいだけのミニゲームをやる自由」「長いだけのコピペダンジョンを探索する自由」。
blocks.translation: “The freedom to have a large number of party members with barely any difference in performance,” “the freedom to buy weak weapons,” “the freedom to play nothing but tedious minigames,” “the freedom to explore nothing but long, copy-and-pasted dungeons.”

blocks.source: そんな自由が充実していたところで、それは下手をすれば「壁に向かって走り続ける自由」「同じ村人に１００回話しかける自由」と大差ないとプレイヤーに思われているかもしれない。
blocks.translation: Even if there is an abundance of such freedom, players may think that, at worst, it is no different from “the freedom to keep running into a wall” or “the freedom to talk to the same villager 100 times.”

blocks.source: 自由は『結果』『反応』あってこそ実感できると言えるだろう。
blocks.translation: It could be said that freedom can only truly be felt when there are “results” and “reactions.”

texts.一般に自由度が高いＲＰＧは良いＲＰＧであると言われることが多い。逆に自由度が低い: RPGs with a high degree of freedom are often considered good RPGs. Conversely, RPGs with little freedom—such as FF13—are frequently criticized as being “linear” or “rail-playing games rather than role-playing games.”
texts.ネット上でのレビューや議論を見る限りでは、どうやらみんな『自由度』が大好きなよう: Judging from reviews and discussions online, it seems that everyone loves “freedom.”
texts.そんな自由度であるが、そこに含まれる『自由』の内実は多岐に渡る。: However, the nature of the “freedom” encompassed by this concept varies widely.
texts.行き先を決める自由: The freedom to choose where to go
texts.誰を仲間にするか決める自由: The freedom to choose whom to recruit
texts.村人に話しかける自由: The freedom to talk to villagers
texts.気に入らないイベントに参加しない自由: The freedom to skip events you do not like
texts.そこで、今一度『自由』というものを細分化しまとめる。自由の内実を理解することで、: So, I would like to break down and summarize the concept of “freedom” once again. By understanding what freedom actually consists of, I want to explore what makes it interesting. Ideally, I would also like to become able to adjust the degree of freedom in ways that make games more interesting.
texts.ゲームにおける自由とは、大きく二つに分けることができる。『目的の自由』と『手段の: Freedom in games can be broadly divided into two types: “freedom of objectives” and “freedom of means.”
texts.プレイヤーが目的を決めることができるという自由。例えば、マルチエンディングの作品: The freedom to choose one’s objectives. For example, in a game with multiple endings, this means being free to decide which ending to pursue.
texts.目的といっても、個別のイベントの目的から、物語の最終目的まで幅広い。洋ゲーなどは: Objectives can range from the goal of an individual event to the story’s ultimate objective. Western games apparently offer a high degree of freedom in this area as well, but I am not familiar enough with them, so I will leave that out.
texts.ポケモンで「ストーリーのクリアはタダの通過点。目的は対戦で勝ちまくることだ！」と: In Pokémon, saying “Clearing the story is just a stepping stone. My goal is to win as many battles as possible!” is also a fine example of freedom of objectives.
texts.ただし、これが全くの自由だと「何をやったら良いのか分からない」という状態になりや: However, be careful: if this freedom is completely unrestricted, players can easily end up not knowing what they are supposed to do. Personally, I sometimes think that if I am going to play a game where “you can do anything,” I might as well pursue creative activities in the real world instead.
texts.やはり、ある程度の方向性は示して欲しいところ。: I still want the game to point me in a general direction.
texts.目的は確定しているものとする。その上で目的を果たすための手段の自由を指す。: Assume that the objective has already been determined. This refers to the freedom to choose the means of accomplishing it.
texts.例えば、敵のボスを「力尽くで倒すか」「トラップを仕掛けてからめ手で倒すか」それと: For example, deciding whether to defeat an enemy boss “by force,” “by setting a trap and using an underhanded tactic,” or “by negotiating and reaching a peaceful agreement.”
texts.潜水機能を持った要塞バンガードを起動するという目的のために、術師の協力を得ること: To achieve the objective of activating Vanguard, a fortress equipped for underwater travel, you must enlist the help of a spellcaster. However, the two most capable spellcasters dislike each other, and neither seems willing to lend their power for free.
texts.取りうる選択肢は以下のようになる。: The available options are as follows.
texts.術師Ａを倒して、術師Ｂの協力を得る。: Defeat Spellcaster A and obtain Spellcaster B’s cooperation.
texts.術師Ｂを倒して、術師Ａの協力を得る。: Defeat Spellcaster B and obtain Spellcaster A’s cooperation.
texts.喧嘩両成敗にして、両方の協力を得る。: Punish both sides equally and obtain the cooperation of both.
texts.終盤のダンジョンである冥府に向かうためには、火山の主と交渉しなくてはならない。「: To reach the late-game dungeon known as the Underworld, you must negotiate with the lord of the volcano. He says, “Bring me the Ice Sword and I’ll let you pass,” but the holy warrior who owns the sword is not likely to give it up easily either.
texts.手段の自由度が高い作品は工夫の余地も大きく、戦略性が高い作品と言えるかもしれない: Games with a high degree of freedom in their means leave plenty of room for ingenuity and could be considered highly strategic. The scenario design is important, but so is the game system and balance.
texts.以下は上に挙げた２つの自由をより詳細に分類したもの。: Below is a more detailed classification of the two types of freedom mentioned above.
texts.掲示された選択肢を選ぶ自由。: The freedom to choose from the options presented.
texts.場合によっては、上に挙げたような目的や手段が変化することもある。: Depending on the situation, the objectives and means mentioned above may also change.
texts.印象的なのはタクティクスオウガ。この作品では要所の選択肢に対する決定によって、以: Tactics Ogre is particularly memorable in this regard. In this game, decisions made at key points can dramatically change what happens afterward.
texts.特に一章最後の選択肢では、主人公が悪事に加担することもできるという内容で、当時衝: The choice at the end of Chapter One was especially shocking at the time, as it allowed the protagonist to become involved in wrongdoing.
texts.このように自分の判断がストーリー展開を大きく左右するということは、プレイヤーの作: When your own decisions have a major impact on the story’s progression in this way, it greatly increases the player’s immersion in the game. Of course, preparing multiple story routes takes a lot of work…
texts.ドラクエによくあるような『はい』だろうが『いいえ』だろうが、会話内容がちょっと変: Choices like those commonly found in Dragon Quest, where answering “Yes” or “No” only slightly changes the dialogue, are of course also part of the “freedom of choice.” Since the outcome does not change, they may not contribute much to the overall degree of freedom, though…
texts.「どれだけ広い範囲を移動できるか」「どれだけ遠くまで移動できるか」「どんな場所に: The freedom to decide “how large an area you can move around in,” “how far you can travel,” and “what kinds of places you can visit.”
texts.ストーリーを進めることで、行動範囲が広がるのが普通だ。特に乗物入手による移動範囲: It is normal for the range of movement to expand as the story progresses. In particular, obtaining a vehicle and thereby expanding the area you can travel is exciting.
texts.自由度が高いＲＰＧは序盤から行動範囲の制約がゆるい傾向にある。これが極めてゆるい: RPGs with a high degree of freedom tend to place few restrictions on movement from the early stages. Games with exceptionally loose restrictions are often called open-world games.
texts.最初から制約はほとんどないが、遠出すると敵が強くなるので実質的には制約があるとい: There is also the Dragon Quest I model: there are almost no restrictions from the beginning, but enemies become stronger when you travel farther, creating practical restrictions.
texts.このタイプの場合、ストーリーを進めなくとも、プレイヤーのスキル次第で遠出できると: The advantage of this type is that, even without progressing the story, players can travel far depending on their skill.
texts.自由度が低いＲＰＧの場合は、前の町に戻ることも満足にできなかったりする。やはりＦ: In RPGs with little freedom, you may not even be able to return properly to previous towns. FF13’s linear progression is once again a representative example.
texts.それに限らず、ストーリー性重視のＲＰＧならば、一時的に行動範囲が狭まった結果、一: More generally, in RPGs that prioritize storytelling, the range of movement may temporarily narrow, making the game more likely to become linear.
texts.移動手段の便利さも重要だ。: The convenience of the available means of transportation is also important.
texts.移動呪文ルーラがあるＤＱシリーズや、ワールドマップを開けば一瞬で各地に移動できる: The Dragon Quest series, with its Zoom spell, and Romancing SaGa, where opening the world map lets you travel anywhere in an instant, are convenient. In recent years, the term “fast travel” has also become commonplace.
texts.前の町に戻るのに、非常に時間がかかるような仕様では、わざわざ面倒をかけてまで戻る: If it takes an extremely long time to return to a previous town, players are unlikely to go back out of their way. This, too, tends to result in gameplay that is nearly linear.
texts.施設／システムを利用する自由: Freedom to Use Facilities and Systems
texts.「お店を始めとした施設を利用できるか」「どんな道具・装備を購入できるか」「転職な: The freedom to choose things such as “whether you can use facilities including shops,” “what items and equipment you can purchase,” “whether you can use systems such as changing jobs,” and “which jobs you can change to.”
texts.ストーリーの進行によって、利用できる『施設／システム』がぎちぎちに定められている: If the facilities and systems available to the player are rigidly restricted according to story progression, the range of possible strategies becomes narrower.
texts.かといって、序盤から何でもできてしまうと、何をやってよいのか分からなくなる。さら: On the other hand, if you can do anything from the beginning, you may not know what you are supposed to do. Another problem is that there may be nothing left to motivate you during the middle and latter parts of the game. This is an important area that requires a good sense of game balance.
texts.イベント等をどんな順番にこなすかを決定する自由。: The freedom to decide the order in which to complete events and the like.
texts.ＤＱシリーズには大抵、オーブなどの何かを自由な順序で集めるイベントがある。ロマサ: The Dragon Quest series usually includes events where you collect something, such as orbs, in any order you like. This also applies to defeating the Seven Heroes in Romancing SaGa 2 and the Four Sinistrals in Romancing SaGa 3. JRPGs with a high degree of freedom often make extensive use of this approach.
texts.「順番を変えられるだけじゃ大したことない」「所詮は朝三暮四」なんて思われるかもし: You may think, “Being able to change the order isn’t a big deal,” or “It’s just a superficial change,” but this is surprisingly significant.
texts.例えば、この自由によってどんなことができるかというと……: For example, here are some things you can do with this freedom...
texts.敵が強いダンジョンにあえて挑んで、パーティを効率良く強化する。: Challenge a dungeon with particularly strong enemies in order to strengthen your party efficiently.
texts.良い武器がある町に優先して向かう。: Prioritize visiting towns that have good weapons.
texts.炎のボスと戦う前に、弱点の氷の武器が手に入るイベントをこなす。ロックマン式。: Complete the event that gives you an ice weapon, the fire boss’s weakness, before fighting it. The Mega Man approach.
texts.気に入った仲間が加わるイベントを優先してこなす。: Prioritize events that add companions you like.
texts.一通り行動できる範囲をブラブラしてみて、面白そうなイベントに挑む。: Wander around the areas you can access and challenge whichever events look interesting.
texts.というように、意外とプレイの幅が広がるものだ。: As you can see, this can broaden the range of gameplay more than you might expect.
texts.もっとも初回プレイではどこで望みの物が手に入るかを把握するのは難しいのだが、色ん: Of course, on your first playthrough it is difficult to know where to find the things you want, but it can be fun to explore various places and feel your way around. From the second playthrough onward, there is also the pleasure of figuring out how to improve your efficiency.
texts.もちろん『行動範囲の自由』が大きいほど、比例してこちらも大きくなるので、合わせて: Naturally, the greater your “freedom of movement,” the greater this freedom becomes as well, so keep the two in mind together.
texts.やってもやらなくてもよいという自由。: The freedom to do something—or not do it.
texts.ゲームクリアに必須ではないサブイベントがこれに当たる。話しかける必要がない町人と: This includes side events that are not necessary to complete the game. Conversations with townspeople whom you do not need to speak to can also be considered part of this category. Although they are optional, their significance changes depending on how important they are.
texts.進行上重要で、こなさないと進行に支障を来たす。: It is important for progressing the game, and failing to complete it interferes with your progress.
texts.例えば「ハッピーエンドのフラグが立たない」「攻略に必要な情報が不足する」など、事: For example, it may be practically semi-mandatory if “the happy ending flag is never set” or “you lack information necessary for completing the game.”
texts.ＤＱ３においては、ラスボス弱体化に必要な『光の玉』の入手イベントがこれに当たる。: In Dragon Quest III, the event where you obtain the “Sphere of Light,” which is needed to weaken the final boss, falls into this category.
texts.重要度が低いと……: When It Is of Low Importance...
texts.別にやらなくてもよい。「強力な装備が手に入るが、無くても十分クリアできる」「キャ: You do not really need to do it. Examples include “you can obtain powerful equipment, but you can easily complete the game without it” and “individual character episodes that have little to do with the main story.”
texts.またまたＤＱ３に例えると、『ノアニール』や『ムオル』のイベントがこれに当たる。そ: To use Dragon Quest III as an example once again, the events in “Noaniels” and “Muor” fall into this category. Sorry to anyone thinking, “I don’t know those events,” or “I forgot about them.”
texts.一般に「自由度が高い作品はゲーム性も高い」と言われる傾向にある。取り得る選択肢が: It is generally said that “games with a high degree of freedom also have strong gameplay.” This is because having many options available also increases the tactical depth. The SaGa series is probably a typical example.
texts.ただし、自由度とゲーム性は必ずしも両立しない。: However, freedom and gameplay do not necessarily go hand in hand.
texts.例えば、あるダンジョンの敵を強くすると必然的に探索が難しくなる。早期の攻略が困難: For example, making the enemies in a dungeon stronger inevitably makes exploration more difficult. In the sense that it makes completing the dungeon early more difficult, this is an adjustment that reduces freedom.
texts.逆に、ダンジョンの敵を弱くすれば自由度は上がるのだが、プレイヤーが攻略する楽しみ: Conversely, weakening the enemies in a dungeon increases freedom, but it also diminishes the fun of overcoming the dungeon. In other words, increasing freedom can result in lower-quality gameplay.
texts.当然ながら「障害がない」ということは「攻略の必要もない」ということでもある。ゲー: Naturally, “having no obstacles” also means “having no need to overcome anything.” If you want to pursue strong gameplay, a certain degree of restriction is necessary.
texts.極端な話をすれば「どのシナリオからでも自由に攻略できます！ 順序による有利不利は: To take this to an extreme, a game design that says, “You can complete any scenario you like! There are no advantages or disadvantages based on order!” will come very close to being “an anthology of short stories whose only distinguishing feature is that they can be played in any order.”
texts.攻略のしがいは薄くなるし、シナリオに順序がないから壮大なストーリーも作りにくい。: There is less incentive to overcome challenges, and because the scenarios have no fixed order, it is also difficult to create an epic story. Creating a game with exciting developments would likely be challenging.
texts.そういう作品もあっていいとは思うけれど、理想のゲームデザインかと言われると考えも: I think it is fine for games like that to exist, but whether they represent an ideal game design is another matter.
texts.自由に対する結果・反応: Results and Responses to Player Freedom
texts.最後に『結果』『反応』の重要性を指摘しておきたい。: Finally, I would like to point out the importance of “results” and “responses.”
texts.自由とは第一にプレイヤーが何をできるかという『入力』である。しかし、入力の方法が: Freedom is first and foremost the “input” of what the player can do. However, simply having many ways to provide input does not necessarily result in a sufficient degree of freedom.
texts.自由度の高さを実感するには、入力に対する『出力』――つまり『結果』『反応』が必要: To truly feel a high degree of freedom, you need “output” in response to the input—in other words, “results” and “responses.” Without enough of this, no matter how many inputs are available, it is only the appearance of freedom.
texts.例を挙げてみよう。: Let me give you an example.
texts.「ＤＱ３の勇者は２１１６８通りの装備ができる！: “The Luminary in Dragon Quest III can equip 21,168 different combinations!
texts.だからＤＱ３の装備は自由度が超高い！」: Therefore, Dragon Quest III’s equipment system offers an incredibly high degree of freedom!”
texts.※ＦＣ版「武器：２１ &times; 鎧：１８ &times; 盾：８ &tim: ※Calculated for the FC version as “Weapons: 21 × Armor: 18 × Shields: 8 × Helmets: 7.”
texts.装飾品は無視。女性専用装備と素手含む。: Accessories are excluded. Female-only equipment and bare hands are included.
texts.恐らく、この主張に納得してくれる人はほとんどいないはず。それは２１１６８の内、意: Presumably, very few people would agree with this claim. That is because only a very limited number of those 21,168 combinations are actually meaningful.
texts.ＤＱ９では装備品によって、キャラクターの見た目が変わるのだが、この時点ではそうい: In Dragon Quest IX, a character’s appearance changes depending on their equipment, but even that kind of element is not present here.
texts.よって、性能に優れた装備だけで固めるのが常となる。: As a result, players generally end up equipping only the equipment with the best performance.
texts.「武器は王者の剣――ただし防具は全裸」: “The weapon is the King’s Sword—but the armor is being completely naked.”
texts.というような珍妙な組み合わせは、最初から選択肢にも入らないというわけだ。: In other words, bizarre combinations like that are not even options to begin with.
texts.要するに自由度が高いとは「プレイヤーが取るに値する行動パターンが豊富にあること」: In short, a high degree of freedom means “having a wide variety of action patterns that are worth choosing for the player.” In that sense, it also has something in common with “strategic depth” and “tactical depth.”
texts.そのためにも、重要なのはバランス調整だ。: That is why balance adjustment is so important.
texts.「性能に大差ない仲間キャラが大量にいる自由」「弱い武器を買う自由」「ダルいだけの: “The freedom to have a large number of party members with barely any difference in performance,” “the freedom to buy weak weapons,” “the freedom to play nothing but tedious minigames,” “the freedom to explore nothing but long, copy-and-pasted dungeons.”
texts.そんな自由が充実していたところで、それは下手をすれば「壁に向かって走り続ける自由: Even if there is an abundance of such freedom, players may think that, at worst, it is no different from “the freedom to keep running into a wall” or “the freedom to talk to the same villager 100 times.”
texts.自由は『結果』『反応』あってこそ実感できると言えるだろう。: It could be said that freedom can only truly be felt when there are “results” and “reactions.”
